SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, September 1, 1931

Marine Engineer Seeks Job
After Siege In Hospital

Leonid von Berg, Russian, hasn't worked in so many months that he is beginning to wonder whether or not there is any work left in the world. Though he has a wife to support, he has drawn exactly 15-12 days' pay since the first of this year.

A capable marine engineer, willing to work at any line, he has worn out the soles of many pairs of shoes pounding Shanghai pavements in search of a job. Financial matters with him are becoming grave. He owes two months rent and no end of medical bills.

Three weeks ago, Leonid obtained a job at Luna Park. The salary wasn't large but it was sufficient to pay the rent and grocery bills. He worked a day and a half and was taken ill. Something was wrong with his ear and he was sent to the Russian charitable hospital on Rue Ratard where he was kept under treatment for a week.

When he left the hospital, his job was gone. He has resumed his daily search for work and without any luck.

Has anyone something for this man to do? He is diligent and industrious. If you have a place in which he can be used, he can be reached through The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury.

海军工程师在医院被围困后求职

列昂尼德·冯·伯格（Leonid von Berg），俄国人，已经好几个月没有工作，以至于他开始怀疑世界上是否还有工作可做。虽然他需要供养妻子，但自今年年初以来，他仅领取了正好15又12天的薪水。

作为一名能干的海洋工程师，他愿意从事任何行业，为了在上海寻找工作，他跑破了多双鞋底。他的财务状况正变得严峻。他拖欠了两个月的房租以及无数的医疗账单。

三周前，列昂尼德在“月神公园”（Luna Park）找到了一份工作。薪水不高，但足以支付房租和杂货账单。他工作了一天半后病倒了。他的耳朵出了毛病，被送往拉塔德路（Rue Ratard）的俄国慈善医院，在那里接受了一周的治疗。

当他离开医院时，他的工作已经没了。他恢复了每日的求职活动，但运气不佳。

有人能给这个人提供工作吗？他勤奋刻苦。如果您有适合他的职位，可以通过《上海晚邮报与水星报》联系到他。

INTELLIGENCE REPORT.

On March 13, a party of police from Wayside Station, acting on information received, arrested a Russian named G. Stambo alias B. Goluboff alias Gorny at No. 15 Dent Road and seized a number of documents, a Soviet naval flag, six automatic pistols and 300 rounds of ammunition which were found in his room. Both Stambo and a room mate of his named G. Belkoff, who was subsequently arrested, will be charged at the Mixed Court on March 15 with being in possession of arms for an unlawful purpose. On being interrogated at Wayside Station, Stambo made a statement, of which a copy is attached, to the effect that the arms came into his possession through the agency of the Soviet Consulate and were intended for use in an attack upon the "White" cruiser "Ohotsk". This statement was partly corroborated by four other Russians who are now detained pending further investigation. Stambo was employed until about three months ago on the "White" newspaper "Russia". The most important of the documents found in his room are :

1. Soviet passport issued to Boris Nikolaevitch Goluboff at Moscow on 13-9-22;

2. Draft of letter to Vice Consul of the U.S.S.R. at Shanghai dated February 28, 1926, enclosing list of Russians who are not only desirous of becoming Soviet citizens but are willing to serve the Soviet Government;

3. Letters, one in Russian and one in English, dated respectively October 8 and 25, 1925, from C.D. Kotori, Hakodate to Goluboff explaining that the former had received a letter from Moscow for the latter;

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of George Stambo alias B. Goluboff alias Gorny.
native of Russia taken by me C. D. J. Ewing
at Wayside on the 13th Mar. and interpreted by D. S. Repas

My name is George Stambo. I am a Russian of Roumanian
origin. I came to Shanghai in September 1925 from Kamchatka
via Hakodate. While employed as chief of a department of the
army on the Polish front in 1922, I secretly signed a petition
protesting against the execution of twenty four socialists who
were followers of Kerensky. Some months later, I was transferred
to Turkestan where I became chief of a labour corps of the army.
These men, while engaged on military service, also performed
manual work. Some months later in the same year, I was trans-
ferred for service in the high school of the commissariat
department of the army in Moscow. A few months after my arrival
there, the news that I had signed the incriminating petition
became known to the authorities, and I was arrested. After
having been detained in gaol for eight months, I was released
for lack of proof. I stopped in Moscow, but was re-arrested
in September 1923. While confined in hospital the following
Spring because of illness, I escaped, and, after changing my
name to Goluboff, I fled to Vladivostock. I worked for some
time on a railway there, and then went to Kamchatka whence I
came to Shanghai. After coming here, I obtained employment
in the "White" newspaper "Russia". I was dissatisfied with
Kolesnikoff, and left that position about three months ago.
Being without employment, I went after Xmas to the Soviet
Consulate and offered to join the Red forces in Kalgan. The
Soviet officials said they had no position for me, but treated
me civilly. I continued to visit the Consulate fairly
frequently in search of a job. I was always received by Minsky,
the Vice Consul. About three weeks ago, I told Minsky that

我叫乔治·斯坦博。我是具有罗马尼亚血统的俄国人。我于1925年9月从堪察加经由函馆来到上海。1922年，当我在波兰前线担任军队某部门主管时，我秘密签署了一份请愿书，抗议处决二十四名克伦斯基追随者的社会主义者。几个月后，我被调往突厥斯坦，在那里成为军队劳工队的队长。这些人除了服兵役外，还从事体力劳动。同年晚些时候，我被调往莫斯科，在军队 commissariat 部门的高中服役。到达那里几个月后，当局得知我签署了那份有罪责的请愿书，我便被捕了。在监狱中被关押八个月后，因证据不足被释放。我留在莫斯科，但在1923年9月再次被捕。次年春天，我因病被关在医院期间逃脱，并将名字改为戈卢博夫，逃往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。我在那里的一条铁路上工作了一段时间，然后去了堪察加，并从那里来到上海。来到这里后，我在“白俄”报纸《俄罗斯报》找到了工作。我对科列斯尼科夫（Kolesnikoff）不满，大约在三个月前离开了那个职位。由于失业，我在圣诞节后去了苏联领事馆，提出加入卡尔干（Kalgan）的红军部队。苏联官员说他们没有职位给我，但对待我很客气。我继续相当频繁地访问领事馆寻找工作。我总是由副领事明斯基（Minsky）接待。大约三周前，我告诉明斯基

31 years of age; Russian; Born in the town of Chistopol;
resident at 1465 Yangtsepoo Road; arrived at Shanghai on March
14, 1923, from Gensan.
Occupation : I served in a foundry in Robison Road.
Participation in the conspiracy :

At the end of February of this year, being without
employment I met one of my acquaintances named Boris Goluboff
and asked him for a job. He promised to assist me but failed
to do so until March 7 when he introduced me to Mr. Sergius
Khlebin resident at No. 9 Dent Road. On the morning of the
following day Goluboff enquired of me what my views were regard-
ing the proposed seizing of the "Ohotsk" and its surrender to
the local Soviet Consulate. According to Goluboff's statement
he conducted the negotiations with the Soviet Consulate who
promised full amnesty for my participation in the seizure of
the steamer and in addition promised me part of the money
allotted by the Soviet Consulate for that work, namely $15,000.
I agreed to his proposal. Goluboff showed me the document
addressed to the Soviet Consulate regarding the proposed seizure
of the "Ohotsk". The document contained the following :-
"In consequence of the proposed Cossack ball which is to take
"place on the 10th of March, a certain number of the crew of
"the Ohotsk are to be on shore and those who remain on board
"who do not desire to join the conspiracy, are to be drugged
"(put to sleep) by means of sleeping powders. At a given signal
"from the steamer a number of the conspirators are to board the
"steamer by means of a ladder that is to be lowered and so seize
"the steamer after which the Soviet flag is to be hoisted."

To the Ambassador of U.S.S.R.
Citizen L.M. Karahan.
Citizen Ambassador !
We, signatories of the present statement, soldiers
defending the military transport "Ohotsk" and their adherents
at Shanghai, consider it the duty of our conscience to
declare to you, Citizen Ambassador, the following :-
The civil war, in which we participated, being drawn
into it, deceived, or led astray by our own fault, threw
us out of the territory of our national land. Years spent
far away from our home have forced us to conclude that we
did wrong. Since then we have had the opportunity to
deeply consider all that has taken place during these years
of bloody struggle. We have been able to closely examine
into the circumstances as to who led us, who guided us
and we have arrived at a true and unmistakable opinion not only
of their actions but also of their motives. Only one thing
can now be clear and incontestible to those people who do
not exclusively seek desires for personal gain and who still
retain even a drop of love for their native land, namely,
that only he fought against the Russian people who again
wishes to drive them into slavery under a Czar and landlords
and again bring them back into darkness and poverty to
become the plaything of the rich.
We realized that we have acted criminally against
our native land. We are convinced that all the aims of
our leaders have been directed exclusively towards fresh
acts of treason.
This conviction has set us on the right path and has
led us to sincerely repent, which we herewith confess.

致苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟大使
L.M. 卡拉汉（L.M. Karahan）公民
大使公民！
我们，本声明的签署人，系在上海保卫军用运输船“鄂霍次克”号（Ohotsk）的士兵及其支持者，认为出于良知的责任，必须向大使公民您声明如下：
我们被卷入、受欺骗或因自身过错被引入歧途而参与的内战，使我们流离于祖国领土之外。远离家园的岁月迫使我们得出结论：我们做错了。自那时起，我们有机会深刻反思这些年血腥斗争中所发生的一切。我们得以仔细审视是谁领导了我们、谁引导了我们，并对他们的行为乃至动机形成了真实且明确的看法。对于那些并非一味追求私利、且仍保留哪怕一丝对故土热爱的人来说，现在只有一件事是清晰且不容辩驳的，即：只有那些希望再次将俄罗斯人民驱入沙皇和地主的奴役之下、重新将他们带回黑暗与贫困之中并使其成为富人玩物的人，才是与俄罗斯人民为敌的。
我们意识到，我们的行为已构成对祖国的犯罪。我们深信，我们领导者的所有目标都完全指向新的叛国行径。
这一信念使我们走上正途，并促使我们真诚悔悟，特此供认。

pages.en:
- 2 -
...request forgiveness and declare that after arriving
...our homes we will be able to efface by our honest labour
...the evil committed by us against our native land.
Having fled from the wrath and revenge of the Russian people our
leaders and guides seized a steamer together with military
and other property belonging to the Russian people.
This property has been squandered in drink and food
and the steamer has been plundered. It has provided our
superiors with several years of joyful life, while we have
led a half starved existence, under a prison rod regime
in the expectation of fresh adventures. And now the fate
of the last steamer, our "Ohotsk" - spared to Russia - has
come. To permit it to be sold would mean to commit fresh
treason, the "Ohotsk" belongs to the Russian people only,
to the Soviet power and not to landlords and generals in
concealment abroad.
We have been spurred exclusively by this conviction
and not the pursuance of any other aims to prevent any further
pillage and make an attempt to seize the "Ohotsk".
We have succeeded. The steamer is in our possession,
we are prepared to defend it from all encroachments and we
request the Representative of Soviet Russia to take it over
from us for his disposal.
We express only the hope that our act will be
valued as the first proof of the sincerity of our declaration
and that we will be given the right to return to our native
land on the "Ohotsk".
13th of March, 1926.
Military Transport "Ohotsk"

为了逃避俄国人民的愤怒与复仇，我们的
领导人和向导劫持了一艘轮船，以及属于
俄国人民的军事和其他财产。
这些财产已被挥霍于酒食之中，
该轮船也遭洗劫。它为我们的
上级提供了几年的享乐生活，而我们则
过着半饥半饱的生活，在监狱般的管制下
期待着新的冒险。如今，最后一艘轮船——“鄂霍次克”号（Ohotsk）——的命运已至，它得以保全并归于俄国。允许将其出售意味着犯下新的叛国罪行，“鄂霍次克”号仅属于俄国人民，
属于苏维埃政权，而不属于隐匿海外的地主和将军们。
我们完全受此信念驱使，而非追求任何其他目标，旨在防止进一步的掠夺，并尝试夺取“鄂霍次克”号。
我们成功了。该轮船现由我们掌控，
我们准备抵御一切侵犯，并恳请
苏俄代表从我们手中接管该船，由其处置。
我们仅希望，我们的行动将被视为
我们声明真诚性的初步证明，
